data.name: 千禧年梦游指南 Guide to the Millennium Dawn
data.detailed_description:
Chinese Dreamcore Theme: A Journey Through "The Past" and "Forgetting"

In Millennium Dream Tour Guide, you plunge into the dreamscape of a major Chinese city from the early 2000s. Pick up that long-discontinued flip phone, capture forgotten scenes, fill your password-protected diary with film photos and stickers, and uncover the truth trapped within the dream. “You can go back, but no one is there anymore.” Will you choose to return to reality, or lose yourself in this endless summer that never fades?

Nostalgic Art Design: An Eternal, Radiant Dreamscape

A unique Chinese Dreamcore art style, paired with meticulously crafted models and textures that build the atmosphere. Blinding afternoon sunlight, blue-tinted glass skyscrapers, newsstands wrapped in plastic magazines, faded wooden furniture. In this deserted yet echoing dream—filled with cicada song and distant laughter—you're transported back to the vibrant, hopeful millennium era when everything felt possible.

Variant Day Gameplay: Fragments of Heart-Wrenching Memories

The entire sprawling city is divided into freely explorable open-world maps. As the story progresses, you'll encounter unique Variant Days, where the city's aesthetic dramatically shifts. You might wander through nationwide celebrations of “Welcome the Olympics, Promote New Trends” and meet cheerful Fuwa mascots; recall the thrill of “I want to be an astronaut—Grandpa and Grandma will be so proud” during the Shenzhou V launch; or navigate bustling red lantern mazes during a lively Spring Festival...

Suspenseful Narrative: A Psychological Game of “Refusing to Grow Up”

You've been diagnosed with Millennium Nightmare Syndrome. The treatment hotline urges you to destroy the dream to awaken. “If you're hearing this message, it means you've been in a coma for over a decade. We're trying a new treatment method, but we can't guarantee success.” “We don't know where this message will appear in your dream… but we sincerely hope you hear it, cooperate with the treatment, and find a way to wake up.” Yet your in-dream diary tells a completely different story. Who is she? Why is she stopping you from waking? As you investigate deeper, you'll uncover the brutal truth behind this collective sleepwalking.

Rich Gameplay Content: A Childhood Amusement Park Ticket You Never Used

“I'll spend a whole day at the amusement park when I grow up.” The child who said that never imagined growing up is a one-way ticket. The dream exists to make up for those missed regrets. Roam freely through the attractions you longed for but never got enough of: bumper cars and inflatable bounce houses in the park, shooting balloons with toy guns on the street, ring toss at roadside stalls—even sneaking into a black internet café to hear the Windows 98 startup chime while searching for traces of the past.

Countless Authentic Details: A Miniature Millennium Nostalgia Museum

We've hidden thousands of era-specific Easter eggs throughout this virtual city. From shelves stocked with fig cookies, crunchy instant noodles, and childhood snacks; to newsstands selling Complete Explanations, Youth Digest, and plastic-wrapped magazines; from TV screens playing Happy Planet and Magic Soldiers, to posters of game movies plastered on walls. Every item has been carefully researched and faithfully recreated, quietly waiting for your camera lens to capture it and paste it into your diary.

  • Processor: Intel Core i5-8400 / AMD Ryzen 5 1600
  • Memory: 16 GB RAM
  • Graphics: NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1060 6GB / AMD Radeon RX 580 8GB
  • DirectX: Version 11
  • Storage: 8 GB available space
